tasks.title: Old Fortran, silent error
tasks.answer:
Because NSUM is not declared, Fortran 77 gives it an implicit type based on its name. Names starting with N are INTEGER by default. So NSUM is an INTEGER, not REAL.

- NSUM = 0.0 assigns 0.0 to an integer: NSUM becomes 0.
- NSUM = NSUM + X(I) mixes integer NSUM with real X(I); the result is real, but then it is assigned back to the INTEGER NSUM, truncating any fractional part.
- After the loop NSUM becomes 3 (integer). RES = NSUM / N uses integer division: 3 / 2 = 1, so RES gets 1.0.

Thus the mean is 1.0 instead of 1.5.

Fix: declare all types explicitly (and use IMPLICIT NONE to catch this), e.g.

- REAL X(*), RES
- INTEGER N, I
- REAL NSUM

Then the computation will be real arithmetic and RES will be 1.5.

Because NSUM is not declared and, by default in Fortran 77, its name NSUM makes it an integer (implicit typing: names starting with N–Z are integer). The line NSUM = NSUM + X(I) adds a real X(I) to an integer NSUM, so NSUM is coerced to real, but then the result is stored back into an integer (truncating the fractional part). After the loop, NSUM is effectively an integer (e.g., 3), and RES = NSUM / N performs integer division (3/2 = 1), which then becomes 1.0 when assigned to RES.

Fix: declare NSUM as real (and add explicit typing to all variables, or use IMPLICIT NONE).

Example corrected code:

SUBROUTINE MEAN(X, N, RES)
  INTEGER N
  REAL X(N), RES
  REAL NSUM
  INTEGER I

  NSUM = 0.0
  DO I = 1, N
     NSUM = NSUM + X(I)
  END DO
  RES = NSUM / N
  RETURN
END

(Optionally add IMPLICIT NONE and declare all variables explicitly for safety.)

With this, X = [1.0, 2.0] yields RES = 1.5 as expected.

Because NSUM is not declared, it is given an implicit type. In Fortran 77, names starting with N are integers. So NSUM is an integer. The statement NSUM = NSUM + X(I) then adds a real X(I) to an integer, producing a real value that is truncated back to an integer. After the first two terms, NSUM becomes 3, and NSUM / N is integer division (3 / 2) = 1. So RES ends up 1.0.

Fix: declare NSUM (and the other variables) with explicit types (and/or enable implicit none).

Example:

SUBROUTINE MEAN(X, N, RES)
      REAL X(N), RES
      INTEGER N, I
      REAL NSUM

      NSUM = 0.0
      DO 10 I = 1, N
         NSUM = NSUM + X(I)
   10 CONTINUE
      RES = NSUM / N
      RETURN
END

(Using IMPLICIT NONE and proper declarations is even safer.)
